title: Component vs Utility Libraries
summary: Compares two ways to style React apps: utility libraries like Tailwind CSS (small classes you combine in your JSX, full design control) and component libraries like React Bootstrap (ready-made styled components, faster to build, less custom). The curriculum says using them is optional but valuable. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Add Tailwind or React Bootstrap to a Vite + React project and explain when you'd pick each.

steps.title: Read both lessons
steps.detail: Read 'Tailwind CSS' and 'React Bootstrap', especially the 'Component Libraries vs Utility Libraries' pros and cons.
steps.doneWhen: You can give one reason to pick Tailwind and one to pick Bootstrap.

steps.title: Try React Bootstrap in a scratch app
steps.detail: Make a throwaway Vite app (not Myflix), install the libraries, import Bootstrap's CSS once at the top of src/main.jsx, then render a <Button> from react-bootstrap.
steps.code:
npm create vite@latest lib-demo -- --template react
cd lib-demo
npm install
npm install react-bootstrap bootstrap
# then add to the top of src/main.jsx:
# import "bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css";
steps.doneWhen: A styled blue Bootstrap button shows up on the page.

steps.title: Compare with Myflix's plain CSS
steps.detail: Myflix styles everything in assignments/week-02/netflix/src/styles/global.css. Pick one ShowCard style rule and write how you'd express it as Tailwind classes (for example rounded-lg shadow-md hover:scale-105). Don't change Myflix yet.
steps.doneWhen: You have a short before/after note for one style.

concepts.meaning: A set of tiny single-purpose classes you combine yourself, like Tailwind.
Ready-made styled components you import, like React Bootstrap's Button or Card.
A class that does one thing, such as p-4 for padding.
Tailwind's md: or lg: in front of a class to apply it only on bigger screens.
